messages:
eli_support: flagged from customer (Acme-Health) — after yesterday's tenant cert rotation they started seeing TLS handshakes hang and intermittent 502s when talking to our private endpoint. they say it started ~2026-02-24 20:17 UTC. sample curl output they pasted: `curl -v https://private.acme.internal/` shows 'SSL: certificate verify failed' then `SSL_ERROR_SSL` and `no peer certificate` on some requests.
jess_support: got the customer timeline + their proxy vendor logs. asked them to repro with `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private.acme.internal:443` and send output, they already sent it. included infirst message.
mike_sre: ping — do we have the rotator job id for that tenant? also did they report any network changes (egress NAT or proxy upgrade) on their side? those symptoms smell like either: (1) truncated chain returned by intermediate-stripping proxy, or (2) OCSP/egress allowlist causing stapling/verification fail.
eli_support: rotator bot shows job id `rot-20260224-8243` applied at 2026-02-24T20:16Z. customer said they restarted their on-prem gateway around the same time. their proxy vendor (vendor-proxy-x) is known to trim chains when configured with `min_chain=true`.
rotator_bot: rotator job rot-20260224-8243: replaced leaf cert and reissued intermediate cross-signed bundle. Full chain uploaded to tenant store. SHA256(leaf)=abcd1234.
ingrid_engineer: can you paste the customer's `s_client` output? need to see chain length and if the intermediate is present. also any OCSP stapled response?
eli_support: pasted the s_client block from customer: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private.acme.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = private.acme.internal
   i:CN = Acme Intermediate CA
---
No client certificate CA names sent
SSL handshake has read 1523 bytes and written 472 bytes
---
```
jess_support: note here the chain only includes leaf and intermediate (no root), but `verify error:num=20` implies the verifier didn't have issuer in its store. customer says their proxy is configured to fetch intermediates from AIA when absent but their appliance had AIA fetch disabled by policy.
mike_sre: that would explain the `unable to get local issuer` but not the intermittent stalls. check OCSP: do we staple OCSP? rotator config for this tenant: `staple: enabled`, but stapled responses TTL was short (30s) in this rotation. if their proxy blocks egress to OCSP responders due to NAT IP allowlist change, stapling refresh could fail and cause synth failures.
eli_support: customer confirmed their NAT egress IP changed during maintenance — they didn't update the allowlist for our OCSP responders. they also said after restart some backend boxes were still serving cached certs (haproxy) without intermediate.
oncall_sre: assigning oncall to validate: @mike_sre please confirm whether we must push immediate hotfix or provide mitigation.
mike_sre: quick mitigation: ask customer to add our OCSP responder IPs to their allowlist and flush proxy cert cache (hot-reload haproxy or restart). alternatively, instruct them to temporarily disable `min_chain`/AIA-fetch restrictions so the proxy will forward the full chain we uploaded.
ingrid_engineer: longer-term fix: rotator should include the full chain and a stapled OCSP blob when pushing to tenant store for Private tenants behind older proxies. I'll open internal ticket and change rotator to emit full-chain-first + 5m-staple fallback. creating ticket RINF-98765.
eli_support: customer asked for repro steps we can share. suggested steps we sent them: 1) run `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private.acme.internal:443` 2) check for presence of intermediate in chain; 3) curl with `--cacert` pointing to intermediate to confirm; 4) test from a host behind same NAT/egress to verify OCSP egress allowed: `curl -v --connect-to private.acme.internal:443 https://private.acme.internal/` 5) restart proxy to clear cached cert chain.
mike_sre: also asked for packet capture of TLS handshake from inside their network if they can provide; look for `Certificate` message length and whether intermediate bytes are present.
eli_support: customer will try allowlist add and proxy restart, will report back within 1h. tagging this thread so eng/sre can follow up. :thumbsup:
ingrid_engineer: I'll schedule a rollout of the rotator change during low-traffic window; ETA for patch: ~48 hours unless they need a hotfix we can push to this tenant sooner.
oncall_sre: noted. created incident link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/RINF-98765 (internal), attaching logs.
eli_support: closing loop for now — will update thread with customer confirmation.
